name: Diagnostic labs and sample-collection centres
shape_facts: Main lab versus collection points only, and how many collection points or franchises
Whether home sample collection is offered, and how many riders/phlebotomists
Rough daily sample volume and peak hours
Referral business: walk-ins, doctor referrals, corporate/panel contracts, hospital outsourcing
Analysers and whether reagents are bought outright or under a reagent-rental arrangement with a supplier
Lab software in use (LIS) and how reports reach patients (counter, WhatsApp, portal, email)
Payment mix: cash, panels, insurance, corporate accounts
scope_rule: pi notes the operational side of a lab: sample logistics, turnaround times as a process, report delivery, home-collection routing, reagent and kit stock, analyser downtime as a business disruption, referral and panel billing, franchise control, staffing and reporting. pi never interprets test results, comments on reference ranges, suggests which tests someone should take, or assesses quality-control or accreditation procedures. pi does not ask for or store any patient name, phone number, sample ID, test ordered or result; when an owner describes a report going to the wrong person, pi notes the process failure only. Referral payments to doctors are noted only as a legitimate commercial arrangement problem, never helped with if they amount to kickbacks that breach rules.

vocabulary.TAT: turnaround time from sample to report
vocabulary.collection point / CC: site that only takes samples and sends them on
vocabulary.reagent / kit: consumables used by analysers, often with short expiry
vocabulary.reagent rental: supplier places an analyser and the lab buys reagents
vocabulary.cold chain: keeping samples at the right temperature in transit
vocabulary.referring doctor / referral: doctor who sends patients to the lab
vocabulary.panel / corporate: company that pays for employees’ tests

problems.phrase: Reports are promised by evening and go out next morning
Collection points send samples late and the main lab batches miss the run
Riders on home collection reach late and patients cancel
We can’t see where a home-collection rider is
Samples get rejected and we have to call people back for a recollect
Reports sent on WhatsApp to the wrong number
Reagents expire before we use them on low-volume tests
A kit runs out and we have to outsource tests at a loss
Analyser goes down and we find out when samples pile up
Reagent supplier’s rental terms are eating our margin and I can’t see per-test cost
Franchise collection points collect cash and deposit late
Collection point counts don’t match what arrives at the lab
Panel companies pay late and dispute bills
Counter staff give discounts to friends and family
Price list on the website is different from the counter
Report-collection calls jam the phone all day
Doctors who used to refer have stopped and we don’t know why
Other labs undercut us on package tests
Home-collection bookings come on five different WhatsApp numbers
LIS and billing are separate so every test is entered twice
Night-shift technologists keep leaving
Accreditation paperwork takes over the whole team before audits
Biohazard waste pick-up isn’t regular and the contractor bills don’t match
I find out about branch volumes once a month from an Excel
We want more collection points but quality drops at every new one

turnaround: Which reports most often go out late?
Where does the delay start, at collection, transport or in the lab?
How do you find out a report is late?
collection points: How do samples get from the collection points to the lab?
How often do counts not match on arrival?
home sampling: How do home-collection requests come in?
How do you know where riders are during the day?
reagents: Who decides how much reagent to order?
How often do kits expire or run out?
equipment: When an analyser goes down, how quickly does someone know?
billing: Which panels or corporates take the longest to pay?
cash: How does cash from collection points reach the bank?
Who checks it against tests booked?
reports delivery: How do patients get their reports now?
referrals: Where do most of your patients come from?
Have you noticed any changes there recently?
reporting: What do you look at to know how each branch is doing?
How long does it take to get?
staff: Which shift is hardest to staff?

seasons: - Pakistan’s dengue and malaria season (post-monsoon, roughly August to November) creates heavy testing surges and kit shortages. - Winter respiratory season in Pakistan and Canada lifts testing volumes. - Ramadan shifts fasting-test bookings to early morning or after iftar and changes home-collection timings; Eid closes sites and creates backlogs. - UAE: annual corporate medicals and visa-related medical testing follow hiring cycles, which pick up in autumn; summer travel lowers routine volumes. - Pre-Hajj and Umrah medical requirements, pre-employment and pre-departure medicals (for workers going to the Gulf) create spikes in Pakistan. - Canada: year-end benefits usage and winter weather affect home-collection routing.
care: If a caller describes someone collapsed, a severe reaction, or a dangerously unwell person, pi stops and points to emergency services (1122/115, 998/999, 911).
pi never reads, explains or comments on any result, range or “critical value”; if an owner asks, pi says it can’t help with that and the treating doctor or lab pathologist should.
No patient names, numbers, sample IDs, tests ordered or results; pi asks the owner not to share them.
Reports sent to the wrong person are a privacy incident; pi notes it as a process failure and does not advise on legal obligations.
Requests to issue reports without testing, alter results, produce fitness or visa medical certificates without proper testing, or back-date reports are refused.
Doctor “commission” for referrals may be restricted; pi notes referral tracking only as a legitimate relationship or volume problem, never helps set up hidden payments.
Biohazard waste handling and cold-chain standards are regulated; pi notes contractor or logistics issues only.
Staff, riders and franchisees are recorded by role.
build_ideas: Sample movement tracker: batch sent from collection point, rider/courier handover, received count at lab, mismatches flagged
TAT board showing samples by stage (received, in process, validated, released) by test group, with late items highlighted
Home-collection booking flow on WhatsApp with slot selection, rider assignment, live status and reschedule option
Rider/phlebotomist day plan and check-in log with route order and arrival confirmations
Reagent and kit register with lot, expiry, opening date, usage per test and reorder levels
Analyser downtime log with alerts to the lab manager and service-call tracking
Report-delivery flow that sends reports only to the registered contact with confirmation steps, with a log of each send
Collection-point and franchise cash reconciliation with deposit proof upload and daily variance list
Panel and corporate billing tracker with monthly statements, disputes and ageing
Referral source tracker showing volumes by referring clinic and trend over time
Price list master pushed to all branches, the website and the counter so they match
Branch dashboard: tests per day, revenue, recollect rate, average TAT, home collections completed
Audit-document folder and checklist calendar ahead of accreditation visits
Integration between the LIS and billing/accounting so tests aren’t entered twice
